# Data Definitions and Mark Sources

Named data definitions load database tables before plots query them. Mark
sources identify the backing table and optional selection filters. Inline mark
arrays bypass the database and cannot be filtered by interactive selections.
See the [runtime loaders](/api/sql/data-loading) for SQL creation and loader options.

## Loaders and Python authoring

| Format | JavaScript loader | Python factory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | `createTable(name, ...)` | `table(query: str)` |
| `parquet` | `loadParquet(name, ...)` | `parquet(file: str, select: Any = None, where: Any = None, **kwargs: Any)` |
| `csv` | `loadCSV(name, ...)` | `csv(file: str, **kwargs: Any)` |
| `json` | `loadJSON(name, ...)` | `json(data: Any = None, file: str \| None = None, **kwargs: Any)` |
| `spatial` | `loadSpatial(name, ...)` | `spatial(file: str, layer: str \| None = None, **kwargs: Any)` |

Python `data(**named_defs: DataDef)` serializes objects exposing `to_dict` and retains
other values. The factories return `DataDef` objects; native frames remain
objects for registration. `parquet` selectively omits `None` for `select` and
`where`, and `spatial` omits an absent `layer`. Other keyword arguments retain
raw spelling and values, including `None`; they can override the emitted type.
`json` can hold data and a file together, although the declarative schema does
not admit that combination. `table(query)` accepts a query only; use a data
definition dictionary when table creation needs extra options.

`source(name, **opts)` returns a `FromRef`, camelizes option names, omits `None`,
and retains false, zero, and empty strings. A string passed directly to a Python
mark denotes a table name. Explicit data bindings choose names; caller discovery
and anonymous `_data0` naming retain frame and definition identity. Python data
factories and `source` keep their historical module and pickle paths.

## Loading behavior and target differences

File inference uses the final suffix without lowercasing or removing query
strings. An explicit type wins over the suffix. Relative file paths resolve
against the supplied `baseURL`; dataset loading follows declaration order.
Spatial definitions enable the `spatial` extension before data loading.
JavaScript applications need a coordinator with a database connector; see
[database connectors](/api/core/connectors).

The original option descriptions below report `temp` and `replace` as defaulting
to true. Current `createTable` and loader implementations default both to false.
With `replace: false`, creation uses
`IF NOT EXISTS` and leaves an existing table unchanged. Set these flags explicitly
when needed.

A `{data: [...]}` definition without a type passes the existing `DataJSONObjects`
schema, while parser inference defaults it to a table definition. Use an
explicit `type: "json"` or a bare array. Empty object arrays pass schema
validation but cannot create a database table without a nonempty column set.
`DataFile` suffixes constrain TypeScript; its wire schema admits any string.

| Native adapter | Applicability |
| --- | --- |
| `unnest` | Native JavaScript and Python sources retain unnest options; the default declarative source schema does not admit this property. |
| `frames` | Python native frames keep their identity for registration and caller naming instead of becoming a wire data definition. |

## DataBaseOptions

Options shared by table and file data definitions.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `Array<string>` | false | A list of column names to extract upon load. Any other columns are omitted. |
| `where` | `string \| Array<string>` | false | A filter (WHERE clause) to apply upon load. Only rows that pass the filter are included. |
| `view` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `false`) to generate a view instead of a table. |
| `temp` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `true`) to generate a temporary view or table. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `true`) to replace an existing table of the same name. If `false`, creating a new table with an existing name raises an error. |

## DataQuery

A SQL query defining a new temporary database table.

```ts
export type DataQuery = string;
```

## DataArray

An inline array of data objects to treat as JSON data.

```ts
export type DataArray = Array<object>;
```

## DataFile

A data definition that loads an external data file.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `Array<string>` | false | A list of column names to extract upon load. Any other columns are omitted. |
| `where` | `string \| Array<string>` | false | A filter (WHERE clause) to apply upon load. Only rows that pass the filter are included. |
| `view` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `false`) to generate a view instead of a table. |
| `temp` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `true`) to generate a temporary view or table. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `true`) to replace an existing table of the same name. If `false`, creating a new table with an existing name raises an error. |
| `file` | ``${string}.parquet` \| `${string}.csv` \| `${string}.json`` | true | The data file to load. If no type option is provided, the file suffix must be one of `.csv`, `.json`, or `.parquet`. |

## DataTable

A data definition that queries an existing table.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `Array<string>` | false | A list of column names to extract upon load. Any other columns are omitted. |
| `where` | `string \| Array<string>` | false | A filter (WHERE clause) to apply upon load. Only rows that pass the filter are included. |
| `view` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `false`) to generate a view instead of a table. |
| `temp` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `true`) to generate a temporary view or table. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | false | Flag (default `true`) to replace an existing table of the same name. If `false`, creating a new table with an existing name raises an error. |
| `type` | `'table'` | true | The data source type. One of: - `"table"`: Define a new table based on a SQL query. - `"csv"`: Load a comma-separated values (CSV) file. - `"json"`: Load JavaScript Object Notation (json) data. - `"parquet"`: Load a Parquet file. - `"spatial"`: Load a spatial data file format via `ST_Read`. |
| `query` | `string` | true | A SQL query string for the desired table data. |

## DataSpatial

A data definition that loads a supported spatial data file format.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `Array<string>` | false | A list of column names to extract upon load. Any other columns are omitted. |

One of: - `"table"`: Define a new table based on a SQL query. - `"csv"`: Load a comma-separated values (CSV) file. - `"json"`: Load JavaScript Object Notation (json) data. - `"parquet"`: Load a Parquet file. - `"spatial"`: Load a spatial data file format via `ST_Read`. |
| `file` | `string` | true | The file path for the spatial dataset to load. See the [DuckDB spatial documentation][1] for more information on supported file types.  [1]: https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial.html#st_read--read-spatial-data-from-files |
| `layer` | `string` | false | The named layer to load from the file. For example, in a TopoJSON file the layer is the named object to extract. For Excel spreadsheet files, the layer is the name of the worksheet to extract. |

## DataDefinition

Supported definitions of a named database table.

```ts
export type DataDefinition = DataQuery | DataArray | DataFile | DataTable | DataParquet | DataCSV | DataSpatial | DataJSON | DataJSONObjects;
```

## PlotDataInline

An array of inline data values to visualize. As this data does not come from a database, it can not be filtered by interactive selections.

```ts
export type PlotDataInline = Array<any>;
```

## PlotFrom

Input data specification for a plot mark.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `string \| ParamRef` | true | The name of the backing data table. |
| `filterBy` | `ParamRef` | false | A selection that filters the mark data. |
| `optimize` | `boolean` | false | A flag (default `true`) to enable any mark-specific query optimizations. If `false`, optimizations are disabled to aid testing and debugging. |

## PlotMarkData

Input data for a marks

```ts
export type PlotMarkData = PlotDataInline | PlotFrom;
```


## Executable starters

File starters use repository fixtures under `data/`: `penguins.csv`,
`penguins.json`, `penguins.parquet`, and `usgs-feed.geojson`. Serve the repository
root for browser examples, or run with the repository as the working directory.
Documentation downloads use the same fixture directory. Install and enable the
DuckDB spatial extension for the spatial example. JSON/YAML examples load through
the specification runtime; JavaScript examples load through a configured
coordinator. Python examples produce serialized definitions for widget execution.

| Variant | Downloads |
| --- | --- |
| `source-filtered` | [JSON](/templates/data/source-filtered.json), [YAML](/templates/data/source-filtered.yaml), [JavaScript](/templates/data/source-filtered.js), <a :href="withBase('/templates/data/source-filtered.py')" download>Python</a> |

The native-only unnest starters are available as
[JavaScript](/templates/data/unnest.js) and
<a :href="withBase('/templates/data/unnest.py')" download>Python</a>.
The <a :href="withBase('/templates/data/frames.py')" download>frame starter</a>
requires PyArrow and demonstrates Python registration; there is no native-frame
JSON/YAML equivalent.
